## Environment

Linux (Fedora 44), Node via repo pnpm, dev servers TRILIUM_ENV=dev tsx src/main.ts, ports 8090 (PR) / 8091 (main)

## Reproduces

yes - two identical fresh databases, identical seeded corpus, query matrix run twice per server with byte-identical output

## Clean profile/database

yes - fresh TRILIUM_DATA_DIR per server, setup via /api/setup/new-document (demo skipped), password via /set-password, ETAPI token via /etapi/auth/login

## Minimal steps

Seeded 45 notes via ETAPI with pinned noteIds on both servers (diacritics, case variants, CJK/Cyrillic/emoji, punctuation-heavy, labels/relations, near-duplicate titles, deep-content, saved search, attribute-equality probes); ran 48-query matrix + 7-query behavior-change battery via GET /etapi/notes?search=...; probed saved-search resolution and quick-search via session-authenticated internal API

## Expected

Baseline (upstream/main @ 916318b3eb) behavior for each differing query, per the tables in Actual below. 42 of 55 ETAPI queries returned byte-identical results on both servers (same membership, same order); those are listed once in the summary and not tabulated.

## Actual

PR behavior (pr10633-search @ 1bfbf79b2a). Convention: expected = baseline result, actual = PR result. Classification is against the PR's stated intent (matching accuracy, content-aware ranking, strict attribute equality, `~=`/`~*` lexer fix).

Run-to-run stability: the full 48-query matrix was executed twice per server; output was byte-identical both times.

### Matching accuracy differences (improvements)

| query | expected (baseline) | actual (PR) | classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cafe` (Q04) | Café de Flore, cafe plain, **.NET Core Guide** | Café de Flore, cafe plain | improvement: baseline fuzzy-matched "Core" (2 edits on a 4-char token); PR's AUTO fuzziness (<=5 chars -> 1 edit) drops the false positive |
| `café` (Q05) | same 3 incl. .NET Core Guide | same 2, no .NET | improvement (same mechanism) |
| `note.title ~= 'plan'` (Q34) | 0 results, silent | 6 results: Project Plan, Project Planning, Project Plans, The Project Plan, cafe plain, project plan archive | improvement: `~=` on properties was dead on baseline (lexer treated `~` as relation prefix, upstream issue 9426); "cafe plain" matches via plain~plan fuzzy, distance 1 |
| `note.title ~* 'progr'` (B5) | 0 results | C++ Programming | improvement: `~*` fragment matching now reaches the parser |
| `#author ~= tolkein` (B6) | Dune, The Hobbit, The Silmarillion | The Hobbit, The Silmarillion | improvement: baseline matched author=Herbert for "tolkein"; PR fuzzy is scoped and sane (transposition distance 1 to Tolkien) |
| `#capital=Vienna` vs label value "Vienna Austria" (B1) | matches Austria Capital | 0 results | improvement per documented semantics (upstream issue 9422): attribute `=` is strict full-value equality again. This is the PR's flagged behavior change; affects ETAPI, saved searches, script APIs |
| `#capital!=Vienna` (B3) | 0 results | Austria Capital | improvement: `!=` complement now consistent with strict `=` |
| `=sync` vs content "please enable (sync) today." (B4) | 0 results | Punctuation Test | improvement: exact-word prefix is punctuation-aware |

### Ranking differences (intended: content matches now score)

| query | expected (baseline order) | actual (PR order) | classification |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apple` (Q01) | APPLE PIE RECIPE, Apple Pie History, apple pie notes, Saved: apple, archived apple document, archived report | Apple Pie History, APPLE PIE RECIPE, apple pie notes, archived apple document, Saved: apple, archived report | intended: promoted notes also contain "apple" in body (RECIPE's body has no "apple"); baseline scored content matches 0 |
| `appl` (Q02) | same as Q01 baseline | same as Q01 PR | intended (same mechanism, prefix tier) |
| `APPLE PIE` (Q11) / `"apple pie"` (Q12) | APPLE PIE RECIPE first | Apple Pie History first | intended but worth noting: History's body contains the exact phrase "apple pie" so it outranks the title-only-plus-partial-content note; exact-case affinity of the query to APPLE PIE RECIPE is not a ranking signal on either branch |
| `"apple` unclosed quote (Q40) | 200, 6 results, order: RECIPE, History, Saved, notes, archived apple document, archived report | 200, same 6 members, order: History, archived apple document, RECIPE, Saved: apple, apple pie notes, archived report | ambiguous: neither branch errors; membership identical; PR's order under a malformed phrase differs from its own plain `apple` order. Cosmetic at worst |

### Saved search and quick search (session-authenticated internal API)

- `/api/search-note/seedSaved1` (saved search `#searchString=apple`): resolves on both; identical 5-note membership; order differs per the ranking change above. PR response adds `highlightedTokenInfos`.
- `/api/quick-search/apple`: identical 6-note membership; order differs the same way; PR adds a `noteId` field to each searchResult entry. Baseline entries carry `notePath` only.

### Identical behavior worth recording (42 queries)

Diacritic folding (zurich/Zürich, strasse/Straße, naive/Naïve, resume), CJK (日本語, 東京), Cyrillic (Москва), emoji (🚀), `C++`, `.NET`, `foo-bar`, dates/numbers, deep-content match (`xylophone729` at end of a ~6 KB body), `#book`, `#book #author=Tolkien` (and lowercase value), `#author!=`, regex `%=`, `*=*`, `=*`, orderBy/orderDirection/limit params, `fastSearch=true` (title hit yes, content hit no), `ancestorNoteId` scoping, `=Dune` exact title, `#capital='Vienna Austria'` quoted full value, malformed `apple (unclosed` (200 + 0 results both), empty search (400 `SEARCH_QUERY_PARAM_MANDATORY` both). `aero` does not match `Ærø` on either branch (Æ is not folded to "ae"; pre-existing, unchanged).

## Scope

Server-side search engine and ETAPI/internal search API, all platforms. Client-side pieces of the PR (results UI cards, jump-to-match, find-bar prefill) were NOT exercised - headless API testing only; those remain untested here. Protected-note search was not exercised. The attribute `=` strictness change (B1/B3) is the one user-visible behavior change that could surprise existing saved searches that depended on the drifted word-match behavior; the PR flags it explicitly.

## Regression

none observed in 55 API queries; all differences align with the PR's stated intent
